sources: https://midnrreservations.com/ (Fort Wilkins Historic State Park campsites via the booking site's /api/maps, /api/resourcelocation/resources and /api/resource/feeDetails for 2026-10-27, 2027-05-18, 2027-07-13 and 2027-09-21; audit/state_park_fees/gtc_probe.py, read 2026-10-25)

values.note: 2027 on the booking site (2027-05-18, 07-13 and 09-21 alike): 20/30-amp sites $37, the nine 50-amp pull-through sites $42. 2026: $35 / $40 (DNR table and booking site). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.

fees.source: https://midnrreservations.com/ feeDetails per fee schedule ($37 / $42 on 2027-05-18, 07-13 and 09-21; $35 / $40 on 2026-10-27) + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/camping-and-lodging-rates-and-operating-dates (Fort Wilkins East & West Campground: 50-amp $40, 20/30-amp $35) + https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/fortwilkins ('A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

hookups.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/fortwilkins ('There are nine 50-amp, pull-through sites on the western end') + midnrreservations.com resources on the 'West' and 'West Extension' maps (69 sites '20 Amps/30 Amps', 9 '20 Amps/30 Amps/50 Amps'; all 'Electric and Water Hookups=Electric Only', 'Sewer Hookup=No'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Sites 101-179 in two loops (DNR); the booking site lists 78 on its 'West 101-139, 161-179' and 'West Extension 140-160' maps. The nine 50-amp pull-throughs (142-158, even numbers) take trailers/RVs to 45 ft; the rest run 20-40 ft, two tent-only.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/fortwilkins ('The West campground (sites #101-179) features two loops with shady sites. There are nine 50-amp, pull-through sites on the western end') + campground map PDF (West Campground, 50AMP PULL-THRU sites 142-158) + midnrreservations.com resources (allowed equipment per site), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Modern restroom with showers between the loops; vault toilets at the east end and by the sanitation station on the entrance road. Laundry is in the East campground. Free WiFi in summer.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/fortwilkins ('A modern restroom with showers is centrally located'; 'In the summer months, free WiFi is available in east and west campgrounds'; 'A laundry facility is available in the east campground') + campground map PDF (West: RESTROOMS, VAULT TOILET(S), SANITATION STATION), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/fortwilkins ('For reservations call 800-447-2757 or reserve online') + DNR rates table (reservation season May 15 - October 14), read 2026-10-25

note: West campground of Fort Wilkins Historic State Park at the tip of the Keweenaw near Copper Harbor, on Lake Fanny Hooe west of the restored 1844 fort: two loops of shady sites with a playground between them; the park's boat ramp and accessible fishing pier are just west. Its own entrance road off US-41, separate from the East campground. --Claude
summary: DNR page + campground and park maps + booking site + DNR rates table: 78 bookable sites 101-179 (count new), nine 50-amp pull-throughs, electric only, lengths to 45 ft (max_rig_ft 50 -> 45); showers/flush and vault toilets/sanitation station/WiFi; reservable. Fees 35-40 (2026) -> 37-42 (2027 booking site). Pin matches OSM's West Campground. Separate entrance from the East loop (~1 km), so the split stands. Season (derived) left: only the reservation season is published. Phone matches. Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Waterfront re-audit lead: the entry is 'not waterfront', but the DNR campground map draws the 50-amp pull-throughs 142-158 and sites 161-179 along the Lake Fanny Hooe shoreline (the DNR page: 'Lake Fanny Hooe is easily accessible from both campgrounds'). Waterfront not changed.

Not a merge: the DNR park map shows the West and East campgrounds on separate roads off US-41 with the fort between them (~1 km apart); the East entry's pin is wrong, though (it sits in this campground; see 3613).
